quick: Ovarian response, signs of OHSS, puberty signs
summary: Human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) mimics luteinizing hormone and is given intramuscularly for prepubertal cryptorchidism, selected male hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, and to trigger ovulation after follicular maturation with menotropins. It is NOT effective for obesity/weight loss. Contraindicated in precocious puberty and androgen-dependent tumors. Main risks are ovarian hyperstimulation and multiple gestation in women.
indications: Prepubertal cryptorchidism not due to anatomical obstruction
Selected cases of hypogonadotropic hypogonadism (secondary to pituitary deficiency) in males
Induction of ovulation and pregnancy in anovulatory infertile women appropriately pretreated with menotropins

dosage.d: 4,000 USP units IM 3 times weekly for 3 weeks
dosage.n: Alternative regimens exist; therapy usually age 4-9 years

dosage.d: 5,000 USP units IM every second day for 4 injections
500-1,000 USP units IM 3 times/week x3 weeks, then twice weekly x3 weeks
dosage.n: Long-course: 4,000 units 3x/week for 6-9 months then 2,000 units

dosage.d: 5,000-10,000 USP units IM, one day after the last menotropin dose
dosage.n: 10,000 units is the labeled trigger dose

admin: Reconstitute with the supplied diluent; use within 60 days and refrigerate after reconstitution
In women, administer only after adequate follicular maturation with menotropins
Do not use for weight loss - it is not effective and not approved for obesity
Withhold the ovulatory dose if there is excessive ovarian response to reduce OHSS risk
moa: hCG is structurally and functionally similar to pituitary luteinizing hormone (LH). It stimulates Leydig cells to produce testosterone (promoting testicular descent and male sexual development) and, in women, triggers final follicular maturation, ovulation and corpus luteum formation/progesterone production.

absolute: Prostatic carcinoma or other androgen-dependent neoplasm
relative: Conditions worsened by fluid retention (asthma, cardiac/renal disease, epilepsy, migraine)
monitor: Ovarian size and estradiol for OHSS
Signs of precocious puberty in boys

preg: Contraindicated in pregnancy; it has no therapeutic role once pregnancy is established and may pose fetal risk.
lact: Use is not recommended during breastfeeding; safety has not been established.
renal: No specific dose adjustment described; use caution where fluid retention could be harmful.

moderate: Menotropins/FSH - additive ovarian stimulation and OHSS/multiple-pregnancy risk (intended combination)
minor: No other clinically significant routine interactions established
interactions.diagnostics: Interferes with pregnancy tests (cross-reacts with hCG assays) for up to ~10 days after administration.

serious: Precocious puberty (in boys treated for cryptorchidism)

monitoring: Ovarian ultrasound and estradiol before the ovulatory trigger to assess OHSS risk
Signs/symptoms of OHSS for ~2 weeks after the trigger
Signs of precocious puberty in boys treated for cryptorchidism
counsel: This is an injection given on a set schedule - keep all appointments
It is not a weight-loss treatment and should not be used for that
Women: report severe bloating, abdominal pain, rapid weight gain or breathlessness urgently
A pregnancy test may be falsely positive for several days after the injection
Report calf pain, swelling or chest pain immediately
pk: LH-like effect within hours; ovulation ~36-40 h after trigger
Serum peak ~6-12 hours after IM dose
Refrigerate (2-8 C) after reconstitution; use within 60 days
pearls: Acts as an LH surrogate - triggers ovulation ~36-40 h after dosing, used to time IUI/retrieval
Explicitly NOT effective for obesity or weight loss (FDA label statement)
Can cause false-positive pregnancy tests for up to ~10 days
Watch for ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome, especially in PCOS/high responders
Contraindicated in precocious puberty and androgen-dependent tumors
missed: Doses are given on a prescribed schedule by or with a clinician; if an injection is missed, contact the clinic for instructions rather than self-adjusting, as timing is critical for the ovulation trigger.
overdose: Overdose is unlikely with recommended regimens; excessive dosing increases the risk of ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome and, in boys, precocious puberty. Management is supportive with monitoring for OHSS and thromboembolism.
